problem.main: Have you ever remembered a song, video, picture, recipe or useful link you saw a few months ago — but couldn’t remember where you saw it or where you saved it? Then begins the frantic search through messages, social media, email, bookmarks and files.
problem.rescue: Here comes Share & Learn to your rescue!

why.heading: What is it?
paragraphs: Keep talking and sharing wherever you normally do.
When something is worth keeping, simply forward it to Share & Learn — an easy way to bring it along without interrupting what you’re doing.
Preserve it, organize it and find it again for yourself, or share it with a community when you choose.

communities.heading: Built around your community
paragraphs: Every community is different. A family might share recipes and memories. A music group might share songs. A learning group might share books, articles and ideas.
You and your community decide what matters.

items.question: What is Share & Learn?
answer: Share & Learn is a community space for keeping and sharing things that are useful, meaningful or worth coming back to — such as songs, recipes, books, useful links, ideas, experiences and more.
Instead of valuable things getting lost over time, they stay connected to the community that shared them.

items.question: Why Share & Learn when we already have other ways to share?
answer: Social media and messaging are great for sharing in the moment, but conversations move on and useful things get buried. Share & Learn helps your community keep what is worth finding again.
Content can stay where it already belongs — on a website, in Google Drive, OneDrive or elsewhere. Share the link as a Bookmark and keep the community knowledge around it in Share & Learn.

points.title: Social media & messaging
points.copy: Great for conversations and sharing in the moment. Share & Learn preserves what is worth finding again after the conversation moves on.

points.title: Google Drive, OneDrive & cloud storage
points.copy: Great for storing files. Share & Learn adds community context, discussion and quick Bookmarks, so members can find what matters without navigating an entire folder hierarchy.

points.title: Email
points.copy: Great for direct communication. Share & Learn keeps useful knowledge from getting scattered across inboxes and long email threads.

points.title: Websites
points.copy: Great for publishing information. Share & Learn brings useful links from many websites together and organizes them around the interests of your community.

points.title: Browser bookmarks
points.copy: Great for saving something for yourself. A browser bookmark says, “I want to remember this.” A Share & Learn Bookmark says, “Our community may find this useful — and here’s why.”

items.closing: Share & Learn doesn’t replace these tools. It gives your community one place to preserve, organize and build knowledge around what is already shared across them.

items.question: What is a Circle?
answer: A Circle is a shared space for a family, group of friends, organization or community.
Every Circle can be different. A family might share recipes and memories, a music group might share songs, while a learning community might share books, articles and ideas.
Each Circle decides what it wants to share and how it wants to organize it.

items.question: What can I share?
answer: That depends on the Circle. A Circle can support different kinds of content, such as Songs, Recipes, Books, Bookmarks, Word Explorer, Fun Facts, Travel experiences, Home Remedies and other content useful to its community.
A Circle doesn’t need to use everything available. Its administrators can choose the content types that make sense for that community.

items.question: What are folders and subfolders for?
answer: Folders help a Circle organize what it shares. They are optional — if a Circle doesn’t need them, members can share items directly in the Circle.

items.question: Why do different kinds of shared items have different information?
answer: Because the information that matters for a recipe isn’t necessarily what matters for a song, book or travel experience. Share & Learn lets each kind of content capture the information that is useful for it.

items.question: Can members discuss what has been shared?
answer: Yes. Members can keep discussions, experiences, tips and other useful context connected to what was shared, instead of having that knowledge disappear into a separate conversation. Over time, an item can become more useful because of what the community contributes around it.

items.question: What is My Library?
answer: My Library is your personal place for keeping track of things in Share & Learn that you want to return to. The original item remains with its Circle.
My Library helps you remember; a shared Bookmark can help your community discover.

items.question: Can I belong to more than one Circle?
answer: Yes. You can belong to different Circles for different families, friends, interests, organizations or communities.

items.question: Who can see what I share?
answer: It depends on the Circle and its access settings. Content shared within a private Circle is intended for members of that Circle.

tutorials.heading: Tutorials
intro: A Circle is who you share with.
A folder is where it belongs.
A content type is what it is.

items.title: Create a Circle
items.intro: A Circle is a shared space for your family, friends, group or community.
steps: Go to Circles and choose + Start a circle. On mobile, choose + New.
Enter a Circle name and a short Description.
Choose an icon and, if you like, add a cover image.
Under What this circle is for, choose the kinds of things your community wants to share. You can change these later.
Choose who can join your Circle: Private, Ask to Join, or Open to All.
Finish creating your Circle. You can then invite people, organize it with folders, and start sharing.
